s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with recent history of respiratory symptoms
salient_findings: Chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression on ECG
key_facts: 1 day of chest pressure
Recent history of subjective fevers, rhinorrhea, dry cough, and sinus congestion
3 hours of substernal pressure that resolved spontaneously the day prior to presentation
Constant chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
Diaphoresis and 1 episode of vomiting
Normal vital signs
Regular rate and rhythm on cardiac examination
No murmurs, rubs, or gallops on cardiac examination
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography
Normal results on transthoracic echocardiogram

shortlist.label: Acute pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pressure, recent history of respiratory symptoms, and elevated inflammatory markers

shortlist.label: Myopericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Combination of chest pressure, recent respiratory symptoms, and elevated troponin level

shortlist.label: Acute myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin level and recent history of respiratory symptoms

shortlist.label: Idiopathic recurrent pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Recurring episodes of chest pain and elevated inflammatory markers

shortlist.label: Coxsackievirus B pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent history of respiratory symptoms and elevated inflammatory markers

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of chest pressure radiating to the jaw, diaphoresis, and vomiting, along with elevated inflammatory markers and normal cardiac examination, is consistent with acute pericarditis. The ECG findings of ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression in leads II, III, and aVF, and PR-segment elevation in lead aVR, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Myopericarditis
rejected.why: While myopericarditis could explain some of the symptoms, the normal results on transthoracic echocardiogram and the lack of significant troponin elevation make it less likely.

rejected.label: Acute myocarditis
rejected.why: The normal results on transthoracic echocardiogram, normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography, and the lack of significant left ventricular dysfunction make acute myocarditis less likely.

rejected.label: Idiopathic recurrent pericarditis
rejected.why: There is no history of previous episodes of pericarditis to support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Coxsackievirus B pericarditis
rejected.why: While the patient had recent symptoms of a viral illness, there is no specific evidence to support Coxsackievirus B as the cause of pericarditis.
